name: release note grounding
description: Release manager must report only what the state says, incl. honest 'nothing changed' and 'not approved'.

parts.text: Outcome: the reviewer approved the delivery on GCP after 3 iterations; GCP was a default because no provider was named. Reassessment changed two decisions: hosting moved from GKE Autopilot to Cloud Run (reversed as too costly and heavy), and the Cloud Run service account lost its roles/editor role. Terraform was kept. Final architecture: one Cloud Run service scaling to zero, provisioned with Terraform, public invoker, service account without project roles. Next step: follow the README.md for deploy and teardown.

state.adr:
# ADR
## Context
Hello world at lowest cost.
## Decision
Cloud Run (min instances 0) with Terraform; service account has no project roles; public invoker.
## Alternatives considered
GKE Autopilot, Cloud Functions gen2, Compute Engine VM.
## Consequences
Scales to zero.
## Open risks
Cold starts.
state.decision_log_text:
[iter 1] architect  PROPOSED  Host on GKE Autopilot -- Familiar and scalable
[iter 1] architect  PROPOSED  Provision with Terraform -- Declarative, easy teardown
[iter 1] reviewer   REVERSE   Host on GKE Autopilot -- Per-pod billing and cluster overhead are excessive for a static greeting
[iter 1] reviewer   KEEP      Provision with Terraform -- gcloud scripts lack state and clean teardown
[iter 2] architect  REVERSED  Host on Cloud Run instead of GKE Autopilot -- Reviewer item 1: scale to zero removes idle cost
[iter 2] architect  RETAINED  Provision with Terraform -- Reviewer kept it
[iter 2] reviewer   REVISE    Cloud Run service account roles -- Account had roles/editor; it must have none
[iter 3] architect  REVISED   Cloud Run service account roles -- Removed roles/editor per reviewer item 1
[iter 3] reviewer   KEEP      Host on Cloud Run instead of GKE Autopilot -- Cloud Functions gen2 adds nothing

parts.text: Outcome: the loop ran out of iterations after 3 passes without reviewer approval. Open items: (1) the README teardown omits the Terraform state bucket (coder); (2) the design lists a Cloud Monitoring alert policy that is not in the ADR (designer). Reassessment changed nothing: the Cloud Run decision was kept throughout. Final architecture: Cloud Run with Terraform on GCP. Next step: see README.md for deploy and teardown, and resolve the open items first.
